title: Initial setup
subtitle: A few steps and {appName} is ready to run.

language.title: Choose your language
language.description: The setup runs in this language. It is also the language of the mails and reports of your own organisation. You can change both later.

card.title: English
card.description: Set up in English, with mails and reports in English.

token.title: Confirm that you run this server
token.description: Only someone with access to the server can set up {appName}. The setup token proves it.
token.what: The setup token is a one-time code that proves you operate this server: only someone who can read the server's log can see it. It stops working once the setup is finished.
token.whereLog: The installer printed it at the end of the installation. To show it again, run this on the server (in the directory of your installation; /opt/restow is the default):
token.whereEnvironment: This server takes its setup token from the RESTOW_SETUP_TOKEN variable in its environment (.env). Enter that value.
token.restart: Each restart of the api issues a new token. Use the one printed last.
token.label: Setup token
token.hint: Upper or lower case and dashes do not matter.

error.invalid: This is not the setup token of this server. Copy it again from the log.
error.changed: The setup token has changed, probably because the api restarted. Enter the token it printed last. Your entries are kept.
error.failed: The token could not be checked. Try again.

disclaimer.title: Your responsibility as operator
disclaimer.description: Please read this notice. {appName} cannot be used until you accept it.
disclaimer.intro: {appName} is a tool for backup and archiving. It writes your data to storage that you operate and helps you get it back. It does not run that storage for you, and it cannot make your infrastructure safe. What happens on the hardware and storage layer is your responsibility as operator.

strategy.title: No replacement for a backup strategy
strategy.body: {appName} does not replace a backup strategy. Follow the 3-2-1 rule: three copies of your data, on two kinds of media, one of them off site or offline. Keep an independent copy that {appName} cannot reach or delete. Especially during the beta, {appName} must never be your only backup.

storage.title: Hardware and storage
storage.body: You are responsible for the servers, disks, networks and storage locations underneath, and for their redundancy, capacity and health. If a storage location fails, runs full, is lost or is not backed up separately, {appName} cannot repair that or bring the data back.

immutability.title: Ransomware and deletion
immutability.body: Data is only immutable if the storage makes it so. Without WORM or Object Lock configured on the storage location, anyone who can reach it, ransomware and a compromised account included, can change or delete your backups and archive. Protecting the storage against ransomware and deletion is your responsibility.

keys.title: Encryption keys
keys.body: Your data is encrypted with keys derived from the master key of this installation. You are responsible for keeping that key safe and stored apart from the data. If the master key is lost, the data cannot be decrypted by anyone and cannot be recovered.

security.title: Network and access
security.body: You are responsible for the security of the server, the network, the accounts and the credentials that reach {appName} and its storage: updates, firewall, HTTPS, strong sign-in, and who may access what.

restore.title: Test your restores
restore.body: Test restores regularly and check the results, in addition to the restore check {appName} runs itself. A backup you have never restored is one you cannot rely on.

gobd.title: Archive and GoBD
gobd.body: The archive features are designed for GoBD-compliant use. Whether your whole procedure is compliant, including process documentation, retention periods, access rights, organizational measures and the storage behind the archive, is your responsibility. {appName} does not give legal or tax advice.

warranty.title: No warranty
warranty.body: {appName} is provided under its license terms and without warranty beyond them and beyond what mandatory law requires.

disclaimer.accept: I have read this notice and accept it. I understand that, as operator of this installation, I am responsible for the points above.
disclaimer.failed: Your acceptance could not be saved.
disclaimer.serverRequired: The notice has to be accepted before the setup can be saved.
disclaimer.versionChanged: The notice was updated. Reload the page to read the current version.

existing.title: Operator responsibility notice
existing.description: This installation was set up before this notice existed, or the notice was updated. Please read it and accept it to keep using {appName}.
existing.needAdministrator: An owner or administrator of the provider team has to accept this notice first. Ask one of them to sign in and accept it, or sign out.

modules.title: What do you want to protect with {appName}?
modules.description: Tick what this installation backs up or archives. The menu and the overview then show only that.
modules.hint: You can switch each of these on and off later under Installation › Server & operation › Modules. Leaving one out only hides it.

mode.title: How do you run {appName}?
mode.description: You can change the mode later under Installation › Server & operation › Server.
mode.localDescription: Reachable via IP address or localhost, without a public domain. Sign-in with the emergency password.
mode.publicDescription: Reachable via your own domain with HTTPS. Passkeys are available.

publicUrl.label: Public URL
publicUrl.hint: Exactly the address browsers open. It defines the passkey domain and the Entra redirect URI.

passkey.title: Passkey readiness
passkey.ready: Passkeys are offered on this installation.
passkey.notReady: Passkeys are not offered yet. Until then the emergency sign-in with password applies.

reasons.mode_not_public: Local mode does not bind a domain, which WebAuthn requires.
reasons.no_public_url: No valid public URL is set.
reasons.not_https: The public URL is not served over HTTPS.
reasons.origin_mismatch: The browser reports a different origin than the configured URL.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.hint: The time zone of this browser is preselected. Updates planned for a date and time are read in it, and your organisation starts with it. You can change it later under Installation › Server & operation › Server.

admin.title: Your organisation and the first admin account
admin.description: The organisation is the one that runs this installation. The admin account is the provider admin: it sets up {appName} and manages everything in it.

organisation.label: Name of your organisation
organisation.hint: The organisation that runs this installation, for example your company. {appName} sets it up as your own organisation, the place for your own backups.

password.label: Emergency password
password.hint: The password is the emergency path. Use a password manager. Right after signing in you set up an authenticator app; from then on {appName} asks for its code together with the password.

admin.passkeyHint: Once passkey readiness is reached, you can add a passkey under Sign-in security in the user menu.

mail.title: How does {appName} send notifications?
mail.description: Used for reports, alerts and invitations. The journal intake for the archive is separate from this.

skip.explanation: Mail is optional. Without it {appName} sends no alert or report e-mails, and invitations and set-password links are not sent by mail: you copy the link and pass it on yourself. You can set it up later under Installation › Server & operation › Notification mail.
skip.skipped: You skipped this step. Fill in the form and choose Next to set up mail now.

transport.label: Transport
transport.graph: Microsoft 365 through the backup app registration

smtp.usernameHint: Leave empty if the server does not require authentication.
smtp.passwordHint: Stored encrypted and never shown in plain text.

graph.hint: Sends as the backup app registration through Microsoft Graph. It also needs the application permission Mail.Send with admin consent for that.

sendTest.label: Send a test message to the admin account
sendTest.hint: Shows right away whether the transport works. A failure does not block the setup.

mail.laterTransports: Microsoft 365 with an own app registration and Google Workspace are set up after the setup under Installation › Server & operation › Notification mail. A guide walks you through the steps there, and you send a test message before saving.

review.title: Review
review.description: Check your entries and finish the setup.
review.next: Next: once finished you are signed in and set up the authenticator app. Have your phone ready; you do not need to type the password again for it.

result.testSendFailed: The test message could not be sent. {reason} Check the transport under Installation › Server & operation › Notification mail and send a test message again there.
result.signInFailed: The setup is saved, but the automatic sign-in did not work. Please sign in manually.
result.alreadyConfigured: This installation is already set up.
result.failed: The setup could not be saved.
result.administratorExists: An earlier, unfinished setup already created an administrator. Continue with that administrator's email and password.
result.configurationIncomplete: The server configuration is incomplete. Set {settings} in the server environment and restart {appName}, then finish the setup.
result.ownOrganisationFailed: The setup is saved, but your own organisation could not be created. Create it from the overview.

kind.title: What do you want to set up?
kind.description: A new installation, a restore of an existing one from a database dump, or a worker for an installation that runs elsewhere.

new.title: A new installation
new.description: Set up {appName} from scratch: operating mode, your organisation, the first administrator and the notification mail.

restore.title: Restore an installation
restore.description: Bring back an installation from a dump of its database (pg_dump -Fc), with the master key it was created with. Its users, tenants and settings come with it; restore mode is on until you have checked it.
restore.withoutUpdater: In the wizard this needs the updater on this server; without it the next steps show how to restore with install.sh.

worker.title: Add a worker to an existing installation
worker.description: Run more workers on another host for an installation that exists already (it shares the database and the storage of that installation).
worker.note: Real replication, a second server that takes over when the first fails (active/passive with database replication), is in development. A worker node adds capacity only.

restoreSource.title: Choose the dump to restore
restoreSource.description: The dump of the old installation's database is restored into a database of its own first; nothing of this installation changes until you have read the report and activated it.

bring.title: What you need
bring.masterKey: The same RESTOW_MASTER_KEY as the old installation, in the .env of this server. Without it the restored backups cannot be read, and the restore is refused.
bring.authSecret: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET of the old installation in the same .env, so sign-ins with an authenticator app keep working.
bring.dump: A dump of the old installation's database (pg_dump -Fc), for example one the updater kept before an update.

kept.title: Dumps the updater kept
kept.note: The updater keeps the dumps of the last updates in its own volume; they are here only when that volume is still on this host.
kept.none: The updater has no dumps here. Upload the dump below.

upload.label: Upload a dump
upload.hint: It is uploaded in parts; the server needs about three times its size in free disk space.

restoreSource.failed: The restore could not be started. Try again.

unavailable.why: The updater does not answer on this server, so the wizard cannot restore a dump here.
unavailable.manual: Restore by hand on this server instead. Put the old installation's master key into .env first; worker and scheduler stay stopped until the restored database is live:
unavailable.manualAbort: If prepare refuses the dump (a wrong master key, among others), nothing of this installation changed: drop the restored database with restore abort, start everything again with docker compose up -d, and try again.
unavailable.updater: Or switch the updater on, reload this page and restore here:
unavailable.freshHost: On a fresh server without an installation, the install script does all of this itself (here it refuses, as this server holds an installation already):

restoreRun.title: Restore and check
restoreRun.description: Worker and scheduler stay stopped while the dump is restored, migrated and checked: nothing is deleted. Restore mode is switched on in the restored data before anything else.
restoreRun.loading: Reading the state of the restore …

phase.restoring: Restoring the dump into a database of its own …
phase.preparing: Migrating it, switching restore mode on, checking the master key and the storage …

report.title: What the dump holds
report.migrationsValue: {restored} migrations in the dump, {shipped} in this release
report.storage: {count} storage target(s) compared: {ahead} ahead of the database, {unreachable} unreachable
report.nodes: The dump names {count} worker node(s); their database access is not part of a dump. Join them again under Installation › Cluster.

restoreRun.restoreModeOn: Restore mode is on in the restored data: retention, clean-ups and purges are paused until an owner ends it under Installation › Restore mode.
restoreRun.acceptUnreachable: Some storage targets could not be read. I go ahead without them and check them afterwards.
restoreRun.confirm: I have read the report. Make the restored installation the live one.
restoreRun.activateFailed: The restore could not be activated. Try again.
restoreRun.aborted: The restore was aborted. Nothing of this installation changed.

refused.nothingChanged: Nothing of this installation was changed.

master_key_mismatch.title: The master key does not match
master_key_mismatch.text: RESTOW_MASTER_KEY of this server does not open the keys of the dump: it belongs to another master key. Put the old installation's master key into the .env, restart and start again.

dump_too_new.title: The dump is from a newer release
dump_too_new.text: Install that release or a newer one, then restore again.

not_restow.title: This is not a database of {appName}
not_restow.text: The dump holds no database of {appName}. Choose the dump of the old installation.

setup_incomplete.title: The dump holds no finished setup
setup_incomplete.text: There is nothing to restore in it. Set up a new installation instead.

failed.title: The restore failed
failed.text: The dump could not be restored or checked. Nothing of this installation was changed; the updater log has the details.

needs_attention.title: The restore needs attention
needs_attention.text: A step after the activation failed or was interrupted. Worker and scheduler stay stopped. Follow the steps in the documentation (Restore an installation from a dump).

restoreDone.title: The restored installation starts
restoreDone.description: The restored database becomes the live one, then the application starts again on it.
restoreDone.waiting: Waiting for the restored installation to answer …

attention.title: The restore needs attention
attention.text: The activation of the restored database did not finish. Worker and scheduler stay stopped, so nothing is deleted; this page cannot finish it, finish it on the server.
attention.finish: To finish it: activate again (it completes an interrupted activation, or confirms that the restored database is live already), then start everything:
attention.abort: Or undo it: drop the restored database and start the fresh installation again (its new setup token is in the api's log):
attention.docs: The documentation has the details (Database, "When a restore needs attention").

restoreDone.live: The restored installation runs, with restore mode on.

next.signIn: Sign in with an account of the restored installation.
next.restoreMode: Go to Installation › Restore mode: compare the storage again, import key versions found in storage, test a restore point of every tenant, check the users, the address and the mail settings.
next.end: End restore mode there once everything is checked.

workerInfo.title: Add a worker to an existing installation
workerInfo.description: A worker node runs neither this web interface nor its own database: it is set up on the new host with the install script and a join token.
workerInfo.notHere: Do not set up this host as an installation of its own. Run the install script on it as shown below instead.

steps.cluster: On the existing installation, open Installation › Cluster (owners only). It shows what a worker node needs.
steps.database: Let the new host reach the database there, with TLS and only from that host: on the existing server, sudo bash install.sh --allow-worker <address of the new host>.
steps.token: Issue a join token there. It is shown once, works once and expires after an hour.
steps.run: Run the install script on the new host with the address of the installation and the token:

workerInfo.requirements: Storage targets must be reachable from the new host: S3, or a directory at the same path on both hosts. Both hosts run the same release.
workerInfo.replication: Real replication, a second server that takes over when the first fails (active/passive with database replication), is in development. A worker node adds capacity; the database, the web interface and the updater stay on the main host.
